title: introduce-soft-surge-silencer-and-regional-stall-mitigation
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Add a 'soft surge silencer' runtime heuristic that temporarily increases per-node fastpath headroom for short, measurable bursts while concurrently marking best-effort tenants for ephemeral regional redirection to standby pools. Motivation: recent incidents showed token-latency spikes due to sudden bursty KV cache thrashing and admission storms; pure hard shedding caused customer-visible 5XXs. The silencer provides a milder, telemetry-driven response window before progressive shedding, reducing SLO breach surface. This PR implements the runtime heuristic, control-plane annotation for tenant priority tagging, a lightweight regional stall detector and an emergency migration shim for low-priority tenants to standby routes. Also includes observability (new metrics and traces), unit and integration tests, and a small hotfix to the regional router to avoid double-redirects. Risk: conservative defaults enabled; feature gated behind runtime flag soft_surge_silencer=true and rollout plan in release notes. Related: ENG-1987 SLO incident postmortem and SUP-3410 customer escalation.

release_notes: Introduces Soft Surge Silencer (runtime flag soft_surge_silencer=false by default). When enabled the runtime provides short headroom boosts for transient bursts and tags low-priority tenants for ephemeral standby redirection before hard shedding. Conservative defaults: 250ms boost window, per-node budget cap. Observability: surge_silencer_active gauge, silencer detection trace spans. Rollout: staged in prod with canary on 5% nodes, monitor surge_silencer_active and token-cost metrics.
